cards.lore: The Sternal Angle (T4/T5) divides the chaos. Trachea bifurcates, aortic arch crosses, SVC forms.
cards.gradeReason: The 4Ts ARE the card. Walk into any viva and you're already performing.

cards.lore: Costophrenic recesses (Ribs 8-12) sit below the lung margin. Fluid pools here first, blunting the angle on an erect CXR.
cards.gradeReason: Negative pressure makes sense but CXR context gates the clinical punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: natural history plate. Subject: stingray floating in negative-pressure fluid bubble. Mood: pressurized serenity.

cards.lore: Right main bronchus is wider and more vertical (25°). Supine aspiration hits the right lower lobe's posterior basal segment.
cards.gradeReason: Aspiration Gravity is a law of physics you can feel tilting right.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pinned moth specimen. Subject: moth wings mapped as bronchopulmonary segments. Mood: taxonomic.

cards.lore: RCA sits in the AV groove, supplying the SA (60%) and AV nodes (90%). Inferior STEMI squint heart block risk.
cards.gradeReason: SA/AV nodes plus STEMI plus heart block — too much packed in for one performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clinical grit illustration. Subject: bulldog with right-dominant coronary artery overlay. Mood: gruff authority.

cards.lore: Irritation of diaphragmatic peritoneum refers pain to the shoulder tip via the phrenic nerve.
cards.gradeReason: Triple Pierce mnemonic with vertebral levels baked in — unstoppable exam weapon.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Art Nouveau anatomy. Subject: manta ray with three glowing diaphragmatic apertures. Mood: sacred geometry.

cards.lore: Vein, Artery, Nerve hide in the subcostal groove. Needles must go OVER the lower rib to avoid disaster.
cards.gradeReason: V-A-N plus 'go OVER' is a complete procedural command in four words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military field manual. Subject: armadillo navigating intercostal space on rib-plated truck. Mood: tactical.

cards.lore: No serosa means early tumor spread. Lower submucosa hosts portal-systemic anastomoses (varices).
cards.gradeReason: Portal bypass is the concept but dual-lore dilutes the performative hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian grotesque. Subject: pelican neck showing three oesophageal constrictions. Mood: stately danger.

cards.lore: SVC obstruction reverses azygos flow. Visible on CXR as right paratracheal widening.
cards.gradeReason: SVC/IVC collateral logic needs imaging context before it activates clinically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: highway propaganda poster. Subject: centipede coiling T12 to T4 as venous highway. Mood: industrial.

cards.lore: Left pulmonary artery arches over the left main bronchus. Therefore, the left hilum sits higher on CXR.
cards.gradeReason: Left hilum higher — you look up on the CXR and know exactly why.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: botanical illustration. Subject: spider weaving hilum anatomy web, eparterial bronchus visible. Mood: precise.

cards.lore: Axillary dissection risks the long thoracic nerve (C5-7). Injury causes a winged scapula.
cards.gradeReason: Sentinel drain is clean but the winged scapula link needs surgical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lymph-sea hybrid illustration. Subject: octopus with axillary node clusters as suckers. Mood: systemic.

cards.lore: Pouch of Douglas (erect) and Morison's pouch (supine) are the lowest points. Free fluid and sepsis collect here.
cards.gradeReason: Pooling logic needs 3D picture of Morison vs Douglas to activate play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bioluminescent cave art. Subject: jellyfish pooling in dependent peritoneal recesses. Mood: gravitational.

cards.lore: Indirect hernias are lateral to inferior epigastric vessels; Direct hernias push straight through Hesselbach's triangle medially.
cards.gradeReason: Hesselbach's breach — lateral vs medial is the only surgical distinction that matters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: construction site cartoon. Subject: badger at triangular road junction with STOP sign. Mood: territorial.

cards.lore: Cirrhosis forces blood through 5 systemic connections: oesophageal, anorectal, umbilical, retroperitoneal, and bare area.
cards.gradeReason: Five valves is a great mnemonic frame but the lore just lists them.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: plumbing diagram creature. Subject: blue worm with five portal pressure blowoff valves. Mood: pressurized.

cards.lore: Segment I (Caudate Lobe) drains directly to the IVC, sparing it in Budd-Chiari syndrome.
cards.gradeReason: Segment I spared in Budd-Chiari — the kind of pearl that wins a viva.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: segmented anatomy chart. Subject: green caterpillar with 8 Couinaud liver segments labelled. Mood: orderly.

cards.lore: Carcinoma of the head causes painless jaundice and a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's sign).
cards.gradeReason: Courvoisier's Grip puts you in the diagnosis room. You feel the gallbladder.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: serpent myth diagram. Subject: snake coiling S-curve around the duodenal C-loop. Mood: elegant danger.

cards.lore: Intimately related to the gastric fundus, left kidney, and tail of pancreas. Splenectomy risks all three.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pinned specimen card. Subject: moth clamped between ribs 9, 10, and 11. Mood: fragile.

cards.lore: Left renal vein crosses anterior to the aorta. Compression by the SMA causes left-sided nutcracker varicocele.
cards.gradeReason: Secondary Stealth describes retroperitoneal anatomy rather than inviting you to embody it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: camouflage manual. Subject: chameleon blending into aortic wall, IVC hidden behind. Mood: concealed.

cards.lore: Griffith's point (splenic flexure) sits between SMA and IMA territories. It is most vulnerable to hypotensive ischaemia.
cards.gradeReason: Watershed point at Griffith's is the exact clinical landmark that saves bowel.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: battle anatomy map. Subject: chess pieces commanding coeliac/SMA/IMA arterial territories. Mood: strategic.

cards.lore: Retrocaecal position masks anterior peritonism but causes a positive Psoas sign on hip extension.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: countdown-fuse poster. Subject: dangling appendix with lit McBurney fuse at 65% angle. Mood: precarious.

cards.lore: Femoral hernias emerge below the inguinal ligament and lateral to the pubic tubercle. The tight ring strangles bowel.
cards.gradeReason: Incarceration Trap — below the ligament, tight ring, bowel dies. Urgency fully embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: escape-room illustration. Subject: chameleon squeezing through femoral ring with bowel visible. Mood: incarcerated.

cards.lore: The puborectalis muscle loops the anorectal junction. Pudendal nerve damage (S2-S4) during childbirth causes prolapse and incontinence.
cards.gradeReason: Puborectalis sling is anatomically specific but performance needs pelvic floor context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: acrobatics anatomy poster. Subject: spider balancing bowling balls in pelvic-floor hammock. Mood: strained control.

cards.lore: Above dentate line: portal venous, visceral pain. Below dentate line: systemic venous, exquisite somatic pain.
cards.gradeReason: Above or below the dentate line changes everything — you know which one hurts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bat anatomy plate. Subject: bat wings divided at dentate line, two pain zones. Mood: dual-tone.

cards.lore: The femoral sheath invests the artery and vein, but the femoral nerve remains outside, laterally.
cards.gradeReason: NAVEL mnemonic works but Cloquet's Weakness is too obscure as the power hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: topographic creature. Subject: diamond-shaped mongoose in NAVEL femoral triangle formation. Mood: geometric precision.

cards.lore: The sciatic nerve exits below the piriformis. Safe IM injection is strictly in the Upper Outer Quadrant.
cards.gradeReason: Upper Outer Quadrant is the only IM injection command you'll ever need.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: danger-zone medical poster. Subject: bear receiving IM injection strictly upper outer quadrant. Mood: cautious authority.

cards.lore: Baker's cyst rupture mimics DVT. Popliteal artery is the deepest structure, right on the femur.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir anatomy illustration. Subject: frog crouching in diamond popliteal fossa, artery deepest. Mood: watchful.

cards.lore: The Anterior Talofibular Ligament (ATFL) is the weakest lateral ligament and most commonly torn in inversion.
cards.gradeReason: TOM CAT needs unpacking before ATFL fires as a usable clinical call.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dance notation anatomy. Subject: flamingo balancing on multicolor ankle ligament arch. Mood: graceful fragility.

cards.lore: The medial meniscus is attached to the MCL (less mobile, easily torn). The lateral is not.
cards.gradeReason: Unhappy Triad — medial meniscus attached to MCL is the one anatomical fact that matters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sports injury diagram. Subject: stork knee with MCL-medial meniscus attachment highlighted. Mood: structural stress.

cards.lore: Pain on passive stretch precedes pulselessness. Fasciotomy must occur within 6 hours to prevent necrosis.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pressure-gauge creature. Subject: puffer fish inside glass fascial box at 30mmHg. Mood: explosive urgency.

cards.lore: Common fibular nerve wraps the fibular neck. Injury causes foot drop and first web space numbness.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dermatome body map. Subject: two snakes coiling limb in L5/S1 dermatome zones. Mood: mapped.

cards.lore: Incompetent perforating veins reverse flow (deep to superficial), causing venous ulcers in the medial ankle gaiter area.
cards.gradeReason: Valve Reversal is correct but the gaiter zone detail needs clinical exposure to play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vascular plumbing diagram. Subject: giraffe with tortuous perforating veins and gaiter zone ulcer. Mood: leaking.

cards.lore: Biopsy in the posterior triangle risks the spinal accessory nerve (CN XI). Injury causes an ipsilateral shoulder drop.
cards.gradeReason: CN XI in the posterior triangle — biopsy warning is real but needs clinical framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: geometry biology illustration. Subject: owl with posterior/anterior neck triangles mapped on plumage. Mood: vigilant.

cards.lore: Right RLN loops the subclavian; Left RLN loops the aortic arch. Inferior thyroid artery ligation risks RLN injury (hoarseness).
cards.gradeReason: Right loops subclavian, left loops arch — trace the nerve with your finger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surgical hazard poster. Subject: butterfly thyroid with RLN loop lightning arc below. Mood: electrified caution.

cards.lore: Lower trunk (C8/T1) injury causes a claw hand and Horner's syndrome (sympathetic disruption).

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nerve root tree illustration. Subject: squid with C5-T1 tentacle roots branching to hand. Mood: complex.

cards.lore: Anterior shoulder dislocation compresses the axillary nerve, causing deltoid weakness and regimental badge numbness.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: axilla cave creature. Subject: bat hanging in axilla with five lymph node clusters visible. Mood: protected.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: carpal anatomy specimen. Subject: crab with LOAF thenar eminence highlighted, ulnar paradox label. Mood: paradoxical.

cards.lore: Supraspinatus initiates abduction (0-15°) but passes tightly under the acromion, risking impingement.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rotator cuff anatomy diagram. Subject: gibbon hanging arm overhead with SITS impingement arc. Mood: impinging.

cards.lore: Supracondylar fracture in children risks the anterior interosseous artery, causing Volkmann's ischaemic contracture.
cards.gradeReason: TAN Formation is useful but Volkmann's contracture needs a fracture scenario to activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: paediatric trauma illustration. Subject: praying mantis with supracondylar nerve compression and claw posture. Mood: urgent.

cards.lore: Scaphoid waist fractures disrupt distal-to-proximal blood flow. Snuffbox tenderness after FOOSH equals fracture.
cards.gradeReason: FOOSH plus snuffbox tenderness plus AVN risk — one complete A&E pearl.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: A&E anatomy chart. Subject: raccoon holding fragmented scaphoid with proximal AVN starvation zone. Mood: retrograde.

cards.lore: Temporal fracture ruptures the middle meningeal artery. Extradural haematoma causes a classic lucid interval before herniation.
cards.gradeReason: Biconvex bleed plus lucid interval — the clinical story tells itself perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: forensic anatomy diagram. Subject: ancient tortoise skull base with biconvex extradural bleed overlay. Mood: lucid interval.

cards.lore: The facial nerve passes through the parotid gland. Aberrant regeneration after surgery causes gustatory sweating (Frey's).

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surgical complication map. Subject: chameleon face with parotid facial nerve branches mapped, sweat drops. Mood: aberrant.

cards.lore: Lumbar facet joints face sagittally, locking out rotation to protect the massive lumbar discs from torsional shear.
cards.gradeReason: Regional Tolerance correctly describes lumbar facets but doesn't invite embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vertebral mechanics diagram. Subject: serpent coiling through sagittal-plane lumbar facets. Mood: constrained rotation.

cards.lore: Lumbar roots exit below the pedicle. A posterolateral disc herniation compresses the traversing root below the disc (e.g., L4/L5 hits L5).

cards.lore: The ligamentum flavum provides the tactile loss of resistance pop indicating entry into the epidural space.
cards.gradeReason: Loss of Resistance is the technique but the card describes more than it performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anaesthesia procedural diagram. Subject: mole burrowing through ligamentum flavum into epidural space. Mood: tactile.

cards.lore: Anterior spinal artery syndrome causes paraplegia and pain loss but spares proprioception (dorsal columns).

cards.lore: The thoracolumbar fascia links the latissimus dorsi to the contralateral gluteus maximus for kinetic transfer.

cards.lore: Anterior cribriform plate fractures tear the olfactory filaments (anosmia) and leak brain fluid (CSF rhinorrhoea).
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon Eyes and Battle's Sign ARE the diagnosis — you see them, you know.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: trauma radiology poster. Subject: woodpecker drilling skull base, raccoon eye rings visible. Mood: diagnostic.

cards.lore: The cricothyroid membrane is the emergency access point. In children, the complete cricoid ring is the narrowest point.
cards.gradeReason: Cricothyroid membrane is the emergency access. This card is a trauma rehearsal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emergency airway anatomy. Subject: ammonite coiling throat to carina at T4/T5. Mood: critical access.

cards.lore: Midline laparotomy cuts the linea alba (avascular cut). McBurney grid iron splits oblique fibres without cutting them.
cards.gradeReason: Avascular planes is the concept but the card explains more than it performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surgical teaching card. Subject: woodpecker drilling layered abdominal wall at McBurney point. Mood: avascular precision.

cards.lore: Ludwig's angina pushes the tongue up, blocking the airway. Retropharyngeal abscesses track directly to the mediastinum.
cards.gradeReason: Ludwig's angina blocks the airway — but full urgency needs clinical framing to fire.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: deep neck danger map. Subject: squirrel descending deep neck spaces to mediastinum. Mood: descending necrosis.

cards.lore: High femoral artery punctures (above inguinal ligament) bleed into the retroperitoneum where they cannot be compressed.
cards.gradeReason: Uncompressible Bleed is the danger — but first you need the anatomy to fear it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: iatrogenic injury warning. Subject: porcupine with quill punctures above inguinal ligament. Mood: retroperitoneal dread.

cards.lore: Cord compression yields lower motor neuron signs at the level, and upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, Babinski) below it.
cards.gradeReason: UMN below, LMN at level — the neurological logic that defines cord compression perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cord compression diagram. Subject: jellyfish disc herniation compressing C5/C6 cervical cord. Mood: split-level signals.

cards.lore: The ureter crosses under the uterine artery. Radical pelvic surgery risks the pelvic splanchnics, causing impotence.
cards.gradeReason: Water Under the Bridge is poetic but pelvic splanchnics lore needs surgical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pelvic anatomy map. Subject: bird in nest with ureteral bridge crossing uterine artery. Mood: surgical caution.

cards.lore: High pulmonary resistance forces blood through the ductus arteriosus. Dropping prostaglandins at birth seal it shut.
cards.gradeReason: Prostaglandin Fall closing the ductus is elegant but needs embryology foundation first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fetal circulation diagram. Subject: translucent tadpole with three glowing fetal shunts closing. Mood: transitional.

cards.lore: Visceral and somatic afferents converge in the dorsal horn. The brain interprets visceral organ agony as skin pain.
cards.gradeReason: Dermatomal Ventriloquism — you'll never mistake T10 appendix pain for skin again.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pain referral map. Subject: parrot pointing to T10 dermatomal chart with appendix highlighted. Mood: ventriloquist.

cards.lore: You don't memorize the clinical sign. You memorize the 3D space, and the clinical sign deduces itself.
cards.gradeReason: Spatial Logic is the right meta-lesson but the card describes rather than performs it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: professor anatomy card. Subject: professorial owl surrounded by floating anatomical diagrams. Mood: integrative.

cards.lore: The body is a Rube Goldberg machine. Destroy the sterile flashcards. Learn the map!
cards.gradeReason: Anatomy Anarchy is pure FrizzleBob manifesto — not a playable card concept.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob universe. Subject: yellow cartoon rabbit at anatomy table with Rube Goldberg body map. Mood: anarchic.

verdict: Gross Anatomy Systems Edition is 56 cards of surgical blueprint delivered as a cast of characters you actually want to meet in a dissection lab. The alliterative naming convention clicks into place like anatomical landmarks: Intercostal Ivan tells you to go OVER the rib before you've finished the power line, Compartment Syndrome Carl radiates a six-hour urgency that no textbook matches. Three cards never quite escape their textbook roots — Back Muscles Barbara, Retroperitoneum Rex, and the closing FrizzleBob meta-card describe anatomy rather than invite you to inhabit it. Minor note: Pleura Percy and Perineum Percy share a surname, as do Varicose Veins Victor and Vertebral Column Victor — shuffled table play could cause confusion. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 cards covering every surgical system from thorax to toe. Each card embodies its anatomy as a named character with a clinical pearl built in — for medical students who want the body to make spatial sense, not just alphabetical sense.

coverQA.coverNote: This cover does everything right for its audience. FrizzleBob at the dissection table with anatomy sketches, a Clinical Anatomy & Physiology textbook, and a pigeon asking 'What the FLUFF?!' signals exactly what's inside. The HUMBUG stamp earns its place as a rebuke of rote learning. No changes needed.

notes: All text is baked into image layers — no text is extractable via PDF tools; vision analysis required for all content. PDF was rendered page-by-page using PyMuPDF at 2x zoom. Dual naming overlap detected: Pleura Percy (card 2) / Perineum Percy (card 22); Varicose Veins Victor (card 30) / Vertebral Column Victor (card 41). Not a critical error but could confuse at table. All 56 cards use consistent layout: named character + subtitle in parentheses + STAT field + POWER + LORE. No RAF dice boxes visible on any card. Artwork throughout is high quality character-matched illustration (creature/animal embodying the anatomical concept). Card 56 (Uncle FrizzleBob's Golden Rule) functions as a philosophical conclusion card — performatively weak but contextually appropriate as a deck-closer.
